entities_included.other: Consolidated statements (Note 1, PDF p.21, printed p.20) cover Harvard Management Company (wholly owned subsidiary), the Faculty of Arts and Sciences, SEAS, the Division of Continuing Education (Harvard Extension School), ten graduate and professional Schools, Radcliffe, museums and the library system. No teaching hospital is consolidated: the report refers to the 'Harvard-affiliated teaching hospitals' as separate organizations (PDF p.23). Sponsored support revenue is $973M in FY25.

calibration_fy23.explanation: FY23 not extracted (FY23 is not in the FY25 report). Only a sanity check is possible: FY24 S&W from the FY25 report is $2,631,642K, +8.7% above the original slide's FY23 figure of $2,421,076K; FY24 core opex under our definition ($5,760,249K) is 2.6% BELOW the original slide's FY23 'core opex' of $5,911,797K, which is consistent with the original slide having used total operating expenses (depreciation and interest left in) rather than the stated definition, the same issue found for the other institutions.

student_counts_in_official_docs: FY25 Financial Report, Note 1, PDF p.21 (printed p.20): 'approximately 7,000 undergraduate and 14,000 graduate students in fiscal year 2025, as compared to 7,100 undergraduate and 13,900 graduate students in fiscal year 2024' = about 21,000 in each year; consistent with the CDS 2024-25 grand total of 21,189 used on the slide.
caveats: Provided by the user, not downloaded: finance.harvard.edu returns Akamai 403 to non-browser clients, so the audited PDF was supplied by Brett. All figures were read from that PDF (pdftotext -layout) and tie: the nine natural-classification lines sum to total operating expenses in both years ($6,794,371K FY25; $6,426,911K FY24).

Students: 21,189 is the Common Data Set fall 2024 grand total, which excludes the Harvard Extension School (Division of Continuing Education), while the expenses include Continuing Education. The FY25 report's own count (about 7,000 + 14,000 = 21,000) matches the CDS. Adding Extension degree students (about 3,600 in fall 2023 per the OIRA fact book) would lower S&W per student by roughly 14%; see the S3_Sensitivity sheet.
Harvard's S&W and benefits lines are clean, separate lines (benefits are 27.4% of S&W in FY25, 26.2% in FY24), so no assumed fringe rate is needed.

Interest ($262.5M) and depreciation ($459.0M) are separate operating lines; 'Fixed asset impairments' ($20.9M FY25) sit inside Other expenses and are NOT removed (the definition removes only depreciation, amortization and interest).
Harvard's total operating expenses are before non-operating items; the FY25 operating deficit is $112.6M (general operating account basis).
